# New renderings — iliad-042 (7.92–180)

Rows for the table in `conventions.md`. Departures from published English: none in wording. 7.92 takes the English the packet shows (the Odyssey unit and 3.95), with ";" for the Greek "·" where the Odyssey unit has "."; the first line of 7.132 and the whole of 7.177 reuse the published wording of iliad-011 and iliad-019 inside units whose other lines are new. 7.174 is word for word 7.119 and has the same English.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀπειλητῆρες (7.96) | "threateners" | "you threateners" | "braggarts", "boasters", "blusterers"; ἀπειλέω keeps "threaten" (1.319, 1.388) |
| αἰνόθεν αἰνῶς (7.97; -θεν ending, sense not known) | "dreadfully, terribly" | "a dreadful, terrible one" (+ note: αἰνόθεν not securely understood) | "from a terrible quarter" (decides the ending), "utterly", "shamefully"; αἰνῶς "terribly" |
| ἀκήριοι (7.100, ἀ- + κῆρ "heart", sense taken from the line) | "spiritless" | "spiritless" (+ note: the Odyssey’s ἀκήριος 12.98 is "uninjured"; formation not certain) | "uninjured" (the Odyssey sense), "heartless" (now means cruel), "cowardly" |
| ἀκλεές (7.100, adverbial) | "ingloriously" | "without glory" | "shamefully", "unknown", "obscure"; ἀ- + κλέος "fame" |
| αὔτως (7.100) | "just so" | "for nothing" | "idly", "in vain" (kept for ἐτώσιος / μάψ), "like this" |
| πείρατα νίκης (7.101–102) | "the limits of victory" | "the limits of victory" | "the outcome", "the ends of victory"; follows the Odyssey’s πείρατα ὀλέθρου "the limits of destruction" and πείρατ’ ἀέθλων "the limit of all our trials" |
| ἔχονται (ἐν ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν, 7.102) | "are held among" | "are held among" | "rest with", "lie with", "hang upon" (each decides the image); ἔχομαι middle-passive of ἔχω "hold" |
| κατεδύσετο τεύχεα καλά (7.103) | "he put on the fine armour" | "put on his fine armour" | "donned", "clad himself in"; τεύχεα καλά "fine armour" (Odyssey 22.114) |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας κατεδύσετο (7.103, whole-line) | "So then, having spoken, he put on the fine armour." | "So he spoke, and put on his fine armour." | follows the table’s ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας "So then having spoken …" / "So he spoke …" |
| βιότοιο τελευτή (7.104) | "the end of life" | "the end of your life" | "the end of livelihood" (βίοτος "life" at 4.170, "livelihood" at 5.544, where it is wealth), "death"; τελευτή "end" |
| ἐν παλάμῃσιν (Ἕκτορος, 7.105) | "in … hands" | "at … hands" | "in the grip of", "in the palms"; παλάμη "hand" as in the table’s παλάμηφιν "palm" / "hand" |
| ἀναΐξαντες ἕλον (7.106, no object stated) | "having sprung up … seized" | "had not sprung up and seized (you)" | "leaping up", "leapt up" (kept for ἀναπηδάω; Odyssey 13.197 turns "leaping up" down), "rushed"; ἀναΐσσω "spring up" (1.584–585) |
| δεξιτερῆς ἕλε χειρός (7.108) | "took … by the right hand" | "took … by the right hand" | "grasped his right hand" (the genitive marks the part taken); follows the table’s δεξιτερῇ "with her right" |
| ἀφροσύνη (ταύτης ἀφροσύνης, 7.110) | "senselessness" | "senselessness" | "folly" (kept for the Odyssey’s ἀφραδίη and ἀτασθαλίαι), "madness", "stupidity"; built on ἄφρων "without wits", as ἀφραίνω "act senselessly" (2.258) |
| οὐδέ τί σε χρή … ἀφροσύνης (7.109–110) | "not at all is there need for you of this senselessness" | "you have no need at all of this senselessness" | "you must not", "it does not behove you"; χρή "need" with the genitive |
| ἀνὰ … σχέο (7.110) | "hold back" | "hold yourself back" | "bear up" (kept for ἀνάσχεο 1.586 "hold out" / "bear up"), "stand back"; ἀνέχω |
| κηδόμενός περ (7.110) | "though you are distressed" | "distressed though you are" | "grieving", "caring" (decide the cause); κήδομαι "be troubled" |
| ἐξ ἔριδος (7.111) | "out of strife" | "out of rivalry" | "in anger", "in quarrel"; ἔρις "strife" |
| στυγέουσι (7.112) | "hate" | "hate" | "loathe", "dread", "shrink from" (the other sense of στυγέω) |
| ἔρριγ’ ἀντιβολῆσαι (7.114) | "shudders to meet" | "shudders to meet him" | "shrinks to meet", "shrinks from meeting", "is afraid to face", "dreads"; ῥιγέω perfect with present sense "shudder", as at 3.259, 3.353; ἀντιβολέω "meet" |
| ἔθνος ἑταίρων (7.115) | "the band of companions" | "the band of your companions" | "tribe", "nation" (the usual later senses), "company", "host", "circle"; ἔθνος "body of people", ἑταῖροι "companions" (2.417) |
| ἀδειής (7.117) | "fearless" | "fearless" | "bold", "unafraid" (kept for ἄφοβος / ἀτάρβητος), "shameless"; ἀ- + δέος "fear" |
| μόθου … ἀκόρητος (7.117) | "insatiate of the fray" | "cannot have enough of the fray" | "battle-din" (kept for φύλοπις), "the press of battle" (turned down at μῶλον 2.401), "the tumult"; μόθος "fray, close fight" |
| γόνυ κάμψειν (7.118) | "bend the knee" | "bend his knee" (+ note: usually taken as rest or relief; the Greek says only "bend the knee") | "rest his knee", "kneel", "fall"; κάμπτω "bend" |
| παρέπεισεν … αἴσιμα παρειπών (7.120–121) | "talked round … speaking things fitting" | "talked … round with what was fitting" | "persuaded", "won over with sound words"; follows the table’s αἴσιμα παρειπών (6.62) "talking him round with what was fitting" |
| γηθόσυνοι (7.122) | "glad" | "glad" | "rejoicing", "joyful"; γηθέω "rejoice" |
| ἀνίστατο καὶ μετέειπεν (7.94, 7.123) | "stood up and spoke among them" | "rose and spoke (among them)" | "rose to speak", "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη); ἀνίστημι "stand up", μετεῖπον "spoke among" |
| ἱππηλάτα Πηλεύς (γέρων ἱππηλάτα, 7.125) | "the old man, horse-driver Peleus" | "Peleus, the old horse-driver" | "old horseman", "horse-taming"; follows the Odyssey’s γέρων ἱππηλάτα Νέστωρ "Nestor, the old horse-driver" |
| οἰμώξειε (7.125) | "would wail" | "would wail aloud" | "groan", "mourn"; οἰμώζω "wail" (5.68) |
| ἐσθλὸς Μυρμιδόνων βουληφόρος ἠδ’ ἀγορητής (7.126) | "good, of the Myrmidons counsel-bearer and speaker" | "that good man, counsellor and speaker of the Myrmidons" | "orator", "wise in counsel"; βουληφόρος "counsel-bearer" / "counsellor" (5.180), ἀγορητής "speaker" (1.248) |
| εἰρόμενος … ἐρέων (7.127–128) | "asking … asking" | "was … glad to question me, asking" | "inquiring", "telling" (decides the verb); εἴρομαι, ἐρέω both "ask" |
| γενεήν τε τόκον τε (7.128) | "the lineage and the birth" | "the lineage and the birth" | "descent and offspring", "stock and children"; γενεή "lineage" (6.145), τόκος "birth" |
| πτώσσοντας (ὑφ’ Ἕκτορι, 7.129) | "cowering" | "cowering" | "crouching", "shrinking"; follows the table’s καταπτώσσοντες "cowering" |
| φίλας ἀνὰ χεῖρας ἀείραι (7.130) | "lift up his dear hands" | "lift his dear hands" | "raise his own hands", "stretch out his hands"; φίλος "dear" |
| θυμὸν ἀπὸ μελέων δῦναι (7.131) | "that his spirit from his limbs might sink" | "that his spirit might leave his limbs and go down" | "that his soul … descend" (ψυχή is "soul"; θυμός stays "spirit"); the infinitive of wish, no verb of praying in the Greek |
| ἡβῷμ’ (7.133) · ἡβώοιμι (7.157) | "I were young" | "I were as young as …" | "in my prime" (loses ἡβάω), "in my youth"; ἡβάω "be in youthful prime" |
| Πύλιοι · Ἀρκάδες (7.134) | "the Pylians" · "the Arcadians" | same | — |
| Κελάδων · Φειά · Ἰάρδανος (7.133, 7.135) | "Celadon" · "Pheia" · "Iardanus" | same | place names transliterated |
| ἐγχεσίμωροι (Ἀρκάδες, 7.134) | "spear-wielding" | "spear-wielding" | Table’s ἐγχεσίμωρος (2.692), unchanged |
| ὠκυρόῳ (Κελάδοντι, 7.133) | "swift-flowing" | "swift-flowing" | Table’s ὠκυρόῳ ποταμῷ (5.598), unchanged |
| Ἐρευθαλίων · Ἀρηΐθοος · Λυκόοργος (7.136–149) | "Ereuthalion" · "Areithous" · "Lycurgus" | same | "Lycoorgus" (the name is spelled "Lycurgus" for Λυκόοργος at 6.130 in iliad-037) |
| τοῖσι δ’ Ἐρευθαλίων πρόμος ἵστατο ἰσόθεος φώς (7.136) | "and against them Ereuthalion stood as champion, a man equal to a god" | "and against them Ereuthalion, a man the equal of a god, took his stand as champion" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος); ἰσόθεος φώς and πρόμος unchanged |
| ἐπίκλησιν κορυνήτην … κίκλησκον (7.138–139) | "by surname club-wielder men called" | "used to call the club-wielder, by surname" | "nicknamed", "styled"; κορυνήτης "club-wielder" (7.9), ἐπίκλησιν "by surname"; κίκλησκον is the imperfect of κικλήσκω, whose -σκ- belongs to the present stem and is not the iterative suffix (so not like μαχέσκετο below), and "used to call" in `i` is taken over from odyssey-088, not from an iterative |
| καλλίζωνοι γυναῖκες (7.139) | "fair-girdled women" | "fair-girdled women" | Odyssey’s καλλίζωνος "fair-girdled", unchanged |

| σιδηρείῃ κορύνῃ (7.141, 7.143–144) | "an iron club" | "an iron club" | "iron mace", "club of iron" |
| φάλαγγας (7.141) | "battle-lines" | "battle-lines" | follows iliad-041 (7.54) |
| δόλῳ (7.142) | "by a trick" | "by a trick" | "by guile" (kept for δολόεις "guileful"), "by treachery", "by cunning" (reserved for μῆτις); δόλος "trick" (Odyssey 5.356) |
| κράτεΐ (7.142) | "by strength" | "by strength" | "by force", "by might" (kept for ἀλκή, μένος); κράτος "strength" |
| στεινωπῷ ἐν ὁδῷ (7.143) | "in a narrow road" | "in a narrow road" | "narrow pass", "narrow way"; στεινωπός "narrow" |
| χραῖσμε (7.144) | "warded off" | "did not ward off" | "availed", "helped", "saved from"; χραισμέω "ward off" |
| ὑποφθάς (7.144) | "forestalling him" | "got in first" | "slipping under", "coming from below" (decides ὑπο-); follows the Odyssey’s ὑποφθαμένη "getting in first" / "forestalling" |
| περόνησεν (7.145) | "pierced" | "pierced" | "spitted", "pinned"; περονάω "pierce" |
| ὕπτιος οὔδει ἐρείσθη (7.145) | "he on his back was driven to the ground" | "was driven down on his back onto the ground" | "fell", "was flung" (keep the passive of ἐρείδω "press, drive", 3.358) |
| τεύχεα … ἐξενάριξε (7.146, armour as object) | "the armour he stripped off" | "he stripped off the armour" | "killed and stripped" (that is the sense with a person as object, 4.488); the verb here has the armour as its object |
| χάλκεος Ἄρης (7.146, the god) | "bronze Ares" | "Ares in bronze" | Table’s χάλκεος Ἄρης (5.704), unchanged |
| μετὰ μῶλον Ἄρηος (7.147) | "into the toil of Ares" | "into the toil of battle" | Table’s μῶλον Ἄρηος (2.401), unchanged |
| ἐγήρα (7.148) | "grew old" | "grew old" | "reached old age"; γηράω |
| θεράποντι φορῆναι (7.149) | "his dear attendant, to wear" | "his dear attendant … to wear" | "servant" (reserved for δμῶς), "squire"; θεράπων "attendant" (2.110) |
| προκαλίζετο … ἀρίστους (7.150) | "kept challenging all the best" | "kept challenging all the best men" | "the bravest"; follows the table’s προκαλίζομαι (4.389) and ἄριστος "best" |

| θυμὸς ἀνῆκε πολυτλήμων (7.152) | "my spirit urged on, much-enduring" | "my much-enduring spirit urged me on" | "stout-hearted", "bold"; ἀνίημι "urge on" (as at 7.25), πολυτλήμων "much-enduring" (Odyssey 18.319) |
| θάρσεϊ ᾧ (7.153) | "in its own boldness" | "in its own boldness" | "in my own courage", "in his boldness"; ᾧ the possessive ὅς agreeing with θυμός |
| γενεῇ δὲ νεώτατος ἔσκον ἁπάντων (7.153) | "in birth the youngest was I of all" | "I was the youngest of them all in age" | "by birth the youngest"; γενεή "birth" here, "in age" in `i` |
| δῶκεν … εὖχος Ἀθήνη (7.154) | "gave me the boast" | "gave me the triumph" | Table’s εὖχος … δώῃ (7.81), unchanged |
| μήκιστον καὶ κάρτιστον (7.155) | "the tallest and strongest" | "the tallest and the strongest" | "greatest", "mightiest" (reserved for ἴφθιμος); μήκιστοι "the tallest" (Odyssey 11.309), κάρτιστοι "the strongest" (1.266) |
| κτάνον (7.155) | "I killed" | "I killed" | "I slew"; unaugmented aorist of κτείνω |

| ἀντήσειε μάχης (7.158) | "meet battle" | "have a fight to face" | "meet me in battle" (supplies the object); ἀντάω takes the genitive |
| προφρονέως (7.160) | "readily" | "readily" | Table’s προφρονέως (5.810), unchanged |
| νείκεσσ’ ὃ γέρων (7.161) | "the old man reviled" | "the old man reviled them" | "rebuked" (kept for νεικεῖ / νείκεε, 1.521, 2.224); follows the Odyssey’s aorist νείκεσσεν "reviled" and 6.325 |
| ἐννέα πάντες ἀνέσταν (7.161) | "nine in all, stood up" | "all nine stood up" | "nine of them"; ἀνέσταν = ἀνέστησαν |
| ὦρτο πολὺ πρῶτος (7.162) | "rose by far the first" | "by far the first to rise" | "sprang up", "leapt up"; ὄρνυμι aorist middle "rise" |

| Αἴαντες (7.164) | "the two Ajaxes" | "the two Ajaxes" | "the Ajaxes"; the plural names the pair, as the dual does at 2.406 |

| ἀτάλαντος Ἐνυαλίῳ ἀνδρειφόντῃ (7.166) | "the equal of Enyalius, killer of men" | same | Table’s ἀτάλαντος Ἐνυαλίῳ (2.651) and ἀνδρειφόντης "killer of men", unchanged |
| Εὐρύπυλος Εὐαίμονος ἀγλαὸς υἱός (7.167) | "Eurypylus, Euaemon’s splendid son" | same | follows iliad-014 (2.736) and 5.79 |
| Ἀνδραιμονίδης (Θόας, 7.168) | "Andraemon’s-son" | "son of Andraemon" | "Andraemon’s son" unhyphenated in `l`; follows Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son" |

| διαμπερές (7.171) | "right through" | "right through" | "to the end", "in turn", "one after another" (each decides what the Greek leaves open); follows the table’s διαμπερές "right through" |
| ὅς κε λάχῃσιν (7.171) | "whoever gets it" | "for whoever is allotted it" | "whoever draws it"; λαγχάνω "obtain by lot" (7.79 λελάχωσι) |
| ὀνήσει · ὀνήσεται (7.172–173) | "will profit" · "will profit" | "will do good to" · "will do good to" | "will help" (kept for ἀρήγω), "will benefit"; follows the table’s ὀνίνημι "profit" (5.205) |

| ἐν δ’ ἔβαλον κυνέῃ (7.176) | "cast in the helmet" | "threw it into the helmet" | "dropped", "put"; κυνέη "helmet" (3.316) |
| λαοὶ δ’ ἠρήσαντο, θεοῖσι δὲ χεῖρας ἀνέσχον (7.177) | published (iliad-019, 3.318) | published | none; the line takes the shipped English unchanged inside a new unit |
| ὧδε δέ τις εἴπεσκεν ἰδὼν εἰς οὐρανὸν εὐρύν (7.178) | "and thus kept saying someone, looking to the wide heaven:" | "and thus would some man say, looking up to the wide heaven:" | "to the broad sky"; first half follows 3.319 (εἴπεσκεν "kept saying" / "would … say"), second half the table’s εἰς οὐρανὸν εὐρύν (3.364) |

| πολυχρύσοιο Μυκήνης (7.180) | "Mycenae rich in gold" | "Mycenae rich in gold" | "golden Mycenae", "wide-streeted" (kept for εὐρυάγυια, 4.52); follows the Odyssey’s πολύχρυσος "rich in gold" |
